fields.description:
## Symptom

Five tests in `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py` fail locally for any
developer whose git config sets `safe.bareRepository = explicit`. They pass under git's default
(`all`), which is what CI uses, so **CI can never exercise this path**. All five fail identically
— not an assertion, a `CalledProcessError` from the test helper: `Command '['git', '-C',
'.../tickets-remote.git', 'ls-tree', ...]' returned non-zero exit status 128`.

## Root cause

`git` refuses to **discover** a bare repository via `-C` / cwd when `safe.bareRepository=explicit`;
it accepts one named by a top-level `--git-dir`. Exit 128 is a refusal to open the repository at
all, *before* any ref lookup:

```
git -C <bare>  -> fatal: cannot use bare repository '<bare>' (safe.bareRepository is 'explicit')
git --git-dir <bare>  -> exit 0
```

The offending helper is `_git` at `test_atomic_completion_close.py:40-46`, which hardcodes
`["git", "-C", str(repo), *args]`. The bare remote is built in `_ticket_remote` (:97-117) and read
at **:401, :402, :415, :423, :435, :455, :493, :576** — eight sites across the five failing
tests.

Two claims in the original report are wrong: the `refs/heads/tickets` ref EXISTS (git never gets
as far as looking it up), and git 2.55.0 is a red herring — `safe.bareRepository` shipped in git
2.38.0 with these exact semantics.

## This is a recurrence of a class already fixed

Closed ticket `3476-4472-3407-4246` (`embolismic-adverse-dragon`) records the policy verbatim:
"the supported test suite must run both locally and in CI. **Treat agents dismissing reproducible
local test failures as environmental noise as an anti-pattern.**" It converted 13 files from
`git -C <bare>` to `git --git-dir <bare>` and added the held-out oracle
`tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py`.

**Why this file escaped the guard:** that oracle pins a **hardcoded allowlist** of 3 fixture nodes
(`_FIXTURE_NODES`). `test_atomic_completion_close.py` was added on 2026-08-25 by commit
`1cb1cdd25aff` — four days *after* the guard landed — and reintroduced the banned construct. There
is no static sweep either, so the guard only checks three files that were already fixed and cannot
fail when a new file reintroduces the defect. **That allowlist is why this is the second
occurrence, and leaving it is why there would be a third.**

## Plan

1. **Point fix.** Add a sibling helper `_bare_git(remote, *args)` that addresses the bare remote
   with a top-level `--git-dir`, and route only the bare-remote call sites through it. `_git` is
   also used on **non-bare** worktrees (`tracker`, `writer`, `tmp_path` for `init`/`clone`), so a
   blanket `-C` -> `--git-dir` swap is wrong. This is the shape ticket 3476 already established in
   the integration fixtures (`_bare_git` beside `_git`).
2. **Close the oracle gap with a tree-derived sweep, inside the guard that failed.** Delete the
   hand-maintained `_FIXTURE_NODES` allowlist from
   `tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py` and replace it with an
   AST sweep over every `tests/**/*.py`. Per module it derives the identifiers bound to a bare
   repository:
   - the last path operand after a `--bare` token (`git init --bare <dir>`, and
     `git clone --bare <src> <dst>`, whose *source* must not be marked);
   - the directory the call runs in when the flag takes no operand (`_git(remote, "init", "-q",
     "--bare")`, the shape the already-fixed integration fixtures use);
   - a name bound by a bare-repository factory: a `bare`-named creator taking only paths
     (`init_bare_remote(remote)`), or a same-module helper that creates a bare repository **and
     returns it** — tracked by return POSITION (`return remote, writer` marks only the first
     element; a helper returning the *worktree* marks nothing) and applied to the **caller's
     binding name**, so a rename (`origin, scribe = _ticket_remote(...)`) is covered;
   - the **argument passed at a parameter position** that the callee marks bare in its own body,
     which covers `_publish_ticket_store(repo, remote)` by dataflow rather than by the caller
     happening to spell the name the same way.
   Marking is otherwise module-scoped by identifier, covering the same flows a second way. Then
   flag any `-C` invocation targeting a marked name — direct, or through a module-local helper
   that forwards its first parameter to `-C`. Two calls are **exempt**: one carrying the inline
   `-c safe.bareRepository=all` opt-in, the deliberate escape ticket 3476 preserved in
   `tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py` (it passes under the strict config today);
   and the **creating** call, since `git -C <dir> init --bare` runs before `<dir>` is a repository.
   Self-test the detector on synthetic offending / renamed-binding / parameter-passed / escaped
   modules, and pin the git behaviour the rule encodes, so neither can rot into a tautology.
3. **Why not a `scripts/check_*.py`.** That is the repo's usual shape for a static sweep and was
   the intended home, but `scripts/_mechanism_delta/detect_ci.py` names every `scripts/check_*.py`
   a `ci_gate` **by its path**, and `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` asserts `new=0` and
   `set(baseline) == live` **regardless of any `# mechanism-ok:` marker** — so a new gate script
   cannot land without an operator running `--lock`. Repairing the existing guard adds no
   mechanism, is the narrower change, and keeps enforcement on the suite CI already runs (a
   portable trigger needing no CI provider of its own).
4. Fix every site the sweep flags, so the guard is green on landing: 12 sites in 2 files — 8 in
   the file under fix and 4 in `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py`, whose
   `test_fresh_clone_json_exposes_allocation_without_a_policy_verdict` and
   `test_invalid_configured_branch_cleans_only_its_temporary_child` fail under the strict config
   today for exactly the same reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `env GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=<file setting safe.bareRepository=explicit> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py` exits 0 with 17 passed (today: 5 failed, 12 passed).
- [ ] The same file still passes under default git config (17 passed), and the full `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle` run still passes.
- [ ] `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py` passes under the strict config too (today: 2 failed, 5 passed) and under the default config.
- [ ] The sweep reports nothing on the fixed tree; reintroducing the `git -C <bare-repo>` construct anywhere under `tests/` makes it fail. Demonstrated by temporarily reverting one call site, observing the guard go RED, and restoring it.
- [ ] The guard's coverage is derived from the tree, not from a hand-maintained file allowlist: `_FIXTURE_NODES` is gone, and a new bare-fixture test using `git -C <bare>` fails the gate with no registration step.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and `pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` all pass, with **no new mechanism registered** — no `# mechanism-ok:` marker needed and no baseline edited.

## Testing

- RED first: `env GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=$STRICT GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 python -m pytest <file> -q` must show `5 failed, 12 passed` before the fix and `17 passed` after, and `2 failed, 5 passed` -> `7 passed` for `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py`.
- Default-config runs of both files, plus `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle -q`.
- Guard: `python -m pytest tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py -q`, plus a mutation run with one call site reverted to `_git(remote, ...)` proving it goes RED.
- Ratchets: `make lint` (module-size, complexity, mechanism-delta), `make typecheck`, and `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py -q` (which `make lint` does NOT cover).
